body:
elaine: quick note 0: we're hitting a lot of idle streaming connections that hold gateway slots for minutes but emit tokens very rarely. this inflates slot counts and kvcache memory. should we split connection vs compute admission?

sam: yes. load tests show same. counts blow up even though GPU work is tiny.

miguel: two problems: admission accounting and kvcache TTLs tied to 'active'. both need to be decoupled.

anya: proposal: conn-slot vs compute-slot. conn-slot is lightweight (fd + tiny state). compute-slot is what we schedule into micro-batches. conn-only streams get a credit pool (e.g., burst credits) that allows occasional token sends without promotion.

ryan: how to handle sudden bursts? need sub-second promotion so UX isn't impacted.

anya: promotion via admission request; if compute available honor within compute_prep_timeout (default 500ms). credits replenish at tenant_credit_rate; when depleted, backpressure clients. SDKs can hint expected bursts via X-Client-Burst header to pre-warm.

sam: pseudo-config suggestion: ```
admission:
  max_compute_slots: 2048
  max_conn_slots: 8192
  tenant_credit_rate: 2/min
  tenant_burst_credits: 6
  compute_prep_timeout_ms: 500
```

miguel: also evict kvcache more aggressively for conn-only streams when credits==0 to save RAM. add to RFC.

elaine: observability requirements: per-tenant conn_slots, compute_slots, credit_balance, promotions, promotion_latency histo, and traces annotated with policy decisions.

anya: feedback to clients: initial 202 + X-Conn-Credits header; when throttled send trailer X-Admit-Status: throttled + Retry-After (for streaming); non-streaming requests get 429.

ryan: billing: recommend tiny per-conn-minute meter for conn-only to deter abuse.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: gateway/edge-credit-admit v0.3 -> edge-canary

elaine: action items: miguel write RFC (state machine + kvcache TTL) EOW; sam add gabby-sim scenarios; anya spec metrics + headers. post abuse examples here.

ryan: incident notes: https://redwood.internal/ops/incidents/2026-03-stream-abuse (internal)

sam: +1

elaine: closing thread once RFC is up.
